new file mode 100644
index 0000000..bbe8d01
--- /dev/null
+++ b/bandit/core/nosec.py
@@ -0,0 +1,283 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Resolve suppression directives before visiting a file's AST.
+
+As with inline nosec comments, None means no suppression and an empty set
+means blanket suppression. Selector evaluation uses ordinary sets internally
+and converts to that convention only after evaluating the entire expression.
+"""
+
+import fnmatch
+import re
+import tokenize
+
+from bandit.core import extension_loader
+
+
+DIRECTIVE = re.compile(
+    r"#\s*nosec-(begin|end|next-line)(?![\w-])(?P<selector>[^#]*)",
+    re.IGNORECASE,
+)
+SELECTOR_TOKEN = re.compile(r"\s+|,|[|&!()\-]|[A-Za-z0-9_*]+")
+
+
+def combine(selectors, enabled=None):
+    """Union suppressions, preserving the blanket and no-effect sentinels."""
+    result = None
+    for selector in selectors:
+        if selector is not None:
+            if not selector:
+                return set()
+            if result is None:
+                result = set()
+            result.update(selector)
+    if result and enabled is not None and result >= enabled:
+        return set()
+    return result
+
+
+class SuppressionMap(dict):
+    """Physical-line regions and position-specific next statements."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.next_statements = {}
+
+    def add_next(self, start, end, selector):
+        for line in range(start[0], end[0] + 1):
+            first = start[1] if line == start[0] else 0
+            last = end[1] if line == end[0] else float("inf")
+            self.next_statements.setdefault(line, []).append(
+                (first, last, selector)
+            )
+
+    def for_position(self, line, column):
+        return combine(
+            selector
+            for first, last, selector in self.next_statements.get(line, [])
+            if column < 0 or first <= column < last
+        )
+
+    def for_node(self, node):
+        if node is None or not hasattr(node, "lineno"):
+            return None
+        return self.for_position(node.lineno, node.col_offset)
+
+
+class SelectorParser:
+    """Set expressions: !, then & and -, then explicit/implicit union."""
+
+    def __init__(self, enabled):
+        self.enabled = set(enabled)
+
+    def atom(self, token):
+        if token.lower() == "all":
+            return self.enabled.copy()
+        if token.lower() == "none":
+            return set()
+        if re.fullmatch(r"B[0-9]*\*?", token, re.IGNORECASE):
+            return {
+                test
+                for test in self.enabled
+                if fnmatch.fnmatchcase(test, token.upper())
+            }
+        test = extension_loader.MANAGER.get_test_id(token)
+        return {test} & self.enabled if test else set()
+
+    def parse(self, expression):
+        if not expression.strip():
+            return set()
+        try:
+            self.tokens = []
+            position = 0
+            separated = False
+            for match in SELECTOR_TOKEN.finditer(expression):
+                if match.start() != position:
+                    raise ValueError("Invalid selector token")
+                position = match.end()
+                token = match.group()
+                if token.isspace() or token == ",":
+                    separated = True
+                    continue
+                if (
+                    self.tokens
+                    and self.tokens[-1] not in {"|", "&", "-", "!", "("}
+                    and token not in {"|", "&", "-", ")"}
+                ):
+                    if not separated:
+                        raise ValueError("Expected selector operator")
+                    self.tokens.append("|")
+                self.tokens.append(token)
+                separated = False
+            if position != len(expression):
+                raise ValueError("Invalid selector token")
+            self.position = 0
+            resolved = self.union()
+            if self.position != len(self.tokens):
+                raise ValueError("Unexpected selector token")
+        except (ValueError, RecursionError):
+            resolved = set()
+            for token in re.split(r"[\s,]+", expression.strip()):
+                resolved.update(self.atom(token))
+        if not resolved:
+            return None
+        return set() if resolved == self.enabled else resolved
+
+    def peek(self):
+        if self.position < len(self.tokens):
+            return self.tokens[self.position]
+        return None
+
+    def unary(self):
+        token = self.peek()
+        self.position += 1
+        if token == "!":
+            return self.enabled - self.unary()
+        if token == "(":
+            result = self.union()
+            if self.peek() != ")":
+                raise ValueError("Unclosed selector group")
+            self.position += 1
+            return result
+        if token is None or token in {"|", "&", "-", ")"}:
+            raise ValueError("Expected selector")
+        return self.atom(token)
+
+    def intersection(self):
+        result = self.unary()
+        while self.peek() in {"&", "-"}:
+            operator = self.peek()
+            self.position += 1
+            right = self.unary()
+            result = result & right if operator == "&" else result - right
+        return result
+
+    def union(self):
+        result = self.intersection()
+        while self.peek() == "|":
+            self.position += 1
+            result |= self.intersection()
+        return result
+
+
+def parse(tokens, lines, enabled, parse_inline):
+    """Build a line map, applying directives to whole logical statements.
+
+    Tokenization keeps directives out of strings and provides logical statement
+    boundaries, including multiline expressions and compound-statement headers.
+    """
+    parser = SelectorParser(enabled)
+    comments = {}
+    statements = []
+    start = None
+    meaningful = False
+    depth = 0
+    ignored = {
+        tokenize.ENCODING,
+        tokenize.INDENT,
+        tokenize.DEDENT,
+        tokenize.NL,
+        tokenize.ENDMARKER,
+    }
+    try:
+        for token in tokens:
+            if token.type == tokenize.COMMENT:
+                comments[token.start[0]] = token.string
+            elif token.type == tokenize.NEWLINE or (
+                token.type == tokenize.OP
+                and token.string == ";"
+                and depth == 0
+            ):
+                if start is not None:
+                    end = (
+                        token.end[0],
+                        (
+                            len(token.line[: token.end[1]].encode("utf-8"))
+                            if token.line
+                            else float("inf")
+                        ),
+                    )
+                    statements.append((start, end, meaningful))
+                start = None
+                meaningful = False
+            elif token.type not in ignored:
+                if start is None:
+                    # AST columns are UTF-8 byte offsets, unlike tokenize's
+                    # character offsets, even for files with other encodings.
+                    start = (
+                        token.start[0],
+                        len(token.line[: token.start[1]].encode("utf-8")),
+                    )
+                if token.type == tokenize.OP and token.string in {
+                    "(",
+                    "[",
+                    "{",
+                }:
+                    depth += 1
+                elif token.type == tokenize.OP and token.string in {
+                    ")",
+                    "]",
+                    "}",
+                }:
+                    depth -= 1
+                if token.string not in {
+                    "(",
+                    ")",
+                    "[",
+                    "]",
+                    "{",
+                    "}",
+                    ";",
+                    "...",
+                }:
+                    meaningful = True
+    except tokenize.TokenError:
+        # The manager handles invalid Python when it builds the AST.
+        pass
+
+    result = SuppressionMap()
+    regions = []
+    pending = []
+    for lineno, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
+        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip(b" \t\f"))
+        regions = [
+            (level, selector)
+            for level, selector in regions
+            if level == 0 or indent >= level
+        ]
+        comment = comments.get(lineno, "")
+        directive = DIRECTIVE.search(comment)
+        kind = directive.group(1).lower() if directive else None
+        if kind == "end" and regions:
+            regions.pop()
+        selectors = [selector for _, selector in regions]
+        if directive is None:
+            selectors.append(parse_inline(comment))
+        selector = combine(selectors, parser.enabled)
+        if selector is not None:
+            result[lineno] = selector
+        if kind in {"begin", "next-line"}:
+            selector = parser.parse(directive.group("selector"))
+            if kind == "begin":
+                regions.append((indent, selector))
+            else:
+                pending.append((lineno, selector))
+
+    # Multiple next-statement directives can target the same statement.
+    statement_index = 0
+    for lineno, selector in pending:
+        while statement_index < len(statements):
+            start, end, meaningful = statements[statement_index]
+            if start[0] > lineno and meaningful:
+                result.add_next(start, end, selector)
+                break
+            statement_index += 1
+
+    for start, end, _ in statements:
+        statement_lines = range(start[0], end[0] + 1)
+        selector = combine(
+            (result.get(line) for line in statement_lines), parser.enabled
+        )
+        if selector is not None:
+            for line in statement_lines:
+                result[line] = selector
+    return result

@@ -119,6 +119,61 @@ as an issue.
 
   assert yaml.load("{}") == []  # nosec assert_used
 
+To suppress a region, use ``# nosec-begin`` and ``# nosec-end``:
+
+.. code-block:: python
+
+  # nosec-begin B602, B607
+  subprocess.Popen('/bin/ls *', shell=True)
+  subprocess.Popen('/bin/echo hello', shell=True)
+  # nosec-end
+
+The region starts on the physical line after ``nosec-begin`` and ends before
+the line containing ``nosec-end``. Regions can be nested; an end directive
+closes the most recently started active region. Extra text after an end
+directive is ignored, and unmatched end directives do nothing. An indented
+region also ends when a later physical line has less leading whitespace than
+the begin line. Otherwise, an unterminated region continues to the end of the
+file. Indentation is measured from the beginning of the line, even when the
+directive follows code.
+
+Use ``# nosec-next-line`` to suppress the next statement:
+
+.. code-block:: python
+
+  # nosec-next-line B602
+
+  # This reviewed call requires a shell.
+  subprocess.Popen(command, shell=True)
+
+Blank lines, comment-only lines, and lines consisting only of grouping tokens
+(``()``, ``[]``, ``{}``), semicolons, or ellipsis literals (``...``) are skipped
+when locating that statement. Suppressions apply to the whole statement,
+including multiline statements. If any line in a statement is suppressed,
+an end directive on a later line of that statement does not undo suppression.
+
+Directive keywords are case-insensitive. The optional selector goes directly
+after ``nosec-begin`` or ``nosec-next-line``, without a keyword prefix:
+
+* An omitted or empty selector, or ``all``, suppresses all enabled tests.
+  ``none`` suppresses nothing.
+* Test IDs and test names select individual tests. A prefix glob such as
+  ``B6*`` selects matching enabled IDs.
+* Spaces, commas, and ``|`` form unions. ``&`` intersects sets, ``-`` subtracts
+  sets, and ``!`` negates a set relative to the enabled tests. Parentheses
+  group expressions. Negation binds first, followed by intersection and
+  difference (left to right), then union.
+* For example, ``# nosec-next-line (B6* - B607) | assert_used`` selects the
+  enabled B6 tests except B607, plus B101.
+* If an expression cannot be parsed, whitespace and comma-separated tokens
+  are treated as a plain union instead.
+
+All applicable suppressions are combined, including inline ``nosec`` comments.
+A blanket suppression takes precedence. A resolved blanket suppression counts
+toward the ``nosec`` metric; a nonempty specific suppression counts toward
+``skipped_tests`` when it suppresses a finding. Empty resolved selections have
+no effect. The ``--ignore-nosec`` option disables all of these suppressions.
+

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+import io
+import textwrap
+import unittest
+
+from bandit.core import config
+from bandit.core import manager
+from bandit.core import nosec
+
+
+class SelectorTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_expressions(self):
+        parser = nosec.SelectorParser({"B101", "B602", "B607"})
+        cases = {
+            "": set(),
+            "   ": set(),
+            "all": set(),
+            "none": None,
+            "B602": {"B602"},
+            "assert_used": {"B101"},
+            "B6*": {"B602", "B607"},
+            "B602,B607": {"B602", "B607"},
+            "B602 B607": {"B602", "B607"},
+            "B602 | B607": {"B602", "B607"},
+            "B6* & B602": {"B602"},
+            "B6* - B602": {"B607"},
+            "!B6*": {"B101"},
+            "!(B602 | B607)": {"B101"},
+            "all - (B602 | B607)": {"B101"},
+            "B101 | B602 & B607": {"B101"},
+            "B101 B602 & B607": {"B101"},
+            "(B101 | B602) & !B607": {"B101", "B602"},
+            "all - all": None,
+            "!none": set(),
+            "B*": set(),
+            "B101 | B6*": set(),
+            "unknown": None,
+            "B999": None,
+            "B602 |": {"B602"},
+            "B602, @bad": {"B602"},
+            "B602 & ( B607": {"B602", "B607"},
+            "B101(B602)": None,
+            "B101!B602": None,
+            "B101 (B602 | B607)": set(),
+        }
+        for expression, expected in cases.items():
+            with self.subTest(expression=expression):
+                self.assertEqual(expected, parser.parse(expression))
+
+    def test_enabled_universe(self):
+        parser = nosec.SelectorParser({"B101", "B602"})
+        self.assertEqual({"B101"}, parser.parse("!B602"))
+        self.assertIsNone(parser.parse("B607"))
+        self.assertEqual(set(), parser.parse("B101 B602"))
+
+
+class DirectiveTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def scan(self, source, ignore=False, include=None):
+        scanner = manager.BanditManager(
+            config.BanditConfig(),
+            "file",
+            ignore_nosec=ignore,
+            profile={"include": include} if include else None,
+        )
+        data = textwrap.dedent(source).lstrip("\n").encode("utf-8")
+        scanner._parse_file("example.py", io.BytesIO(data), ["example.py"])
+        self.assertEqual([], scanner.skipped)
+        return scanner
+
+    def check(self, source, lines, nosec_count=0, specific=0, **kwargs):
+        scanner = self.scan(source, **kwargs)
+        self.assertEqual(lines, [result.lineno for result in scanner.results])
+        metrics = scanner.metrics.data["example.py"]
+        self.assertEqual(nosec_count, metrics["nosec"])
+        self.assertEqual(specific, metrics["skipped_tests"])
+        return scanner
+
+    def test_region_boundaries(self):
+        self.check(
+            """
+            assert True  # nosec-begin B101
+            assert True
+            assert True  # nosec-end extra text B101
+            assert True
+        """,
+            [1, 3, 4],
+            specific=1,
+        )
+
+    def test_case_insensitive(self):
+        self.check(
+            """
+            # NoSeC-BeGiN B101
+            assert True
+            # NOSEC-END
+            # NoSeC-NeXt-LiNe assert_used
+            assert True
+            assert True  # NOSEC
+            assert True
+        """,
+            [7],
+            nosec_count=1,
+            specific=2,
+        )
+
+    def test_unterminated_regions(self):
+        self.check(
+            """
+            # nosec-begin
+            assert True
+            assert True
+        """,
+            [],
+            nosec_count=2,
+        )
+
+    def test_indented_region_dedents(self):
+        self.check(
+            """
+            def f():
+                # nosec-begin B101
+                assert True
+            assert True
+        """,
+            [4],
+            specific=1,
+        )
+
+    def test_inline_begin_uses_leading_indent(self):
+        self.check(
+            """
+            def f():
+                assert True  # nosec-begin B101
+                assert True
+            assert True
+        """,
+            [2, 4],
+            specific=1,
+        )
+
+    def test_tabs_and_nested_dedent(self):
+        self.check(
+            "# nosec-begin B101\n"
+            "def f():\n"
+            "\t# nosec-begin all\n"
+            "\tassert True\n"
+            "assert True\n"
+            "# nosec-end\n"
+            "assert True\n",
+            [7],
+            nosec_count=1,
+            specific=1,
+        )
+
+    def test_blank_physical_line_dedents_region(self):
+        self.check(
+            """
+            def f():
+                # nosec-begin
+                assert True
+
+                assert True
+        """,
+            [5],
+            nosec_count=1,
+        )
+
+    def test_nested_regions_and_unmatched_end(self):
+        self.check(
+            """
+            # nosec-end
+            # nosec-begin B101
+            # nosec-begin none
+            assert True
+            # nosec-end
+            assert True
+            # nosec-end
+            assert True
+            # nosec-end
+            assert True
+        """,
+            [8, 10],
+            specific=2,
+        )
+
+    def test_next_skips_non_statements(self):
+        self.check(
+            """
+            # nosec-next-line B101
+
+            # ordinary comment
+            (...); []
+            {}
+            assert (
+                True
+            )
+            assert True
+        """,
+            [9],
+            specific=1,
+        )
+
+    def test_next_skips_grouping_lines_in_target(self):
+        self.check(
+            """
+            # nosec-next-line B307
+            (
+                (
+                    eval('1')
+                )
+            )
+            eval('2')
+        """,
+            [7],
+            specific=1,
+        )
+
+    def test_next_only_first_semicolon_statement(self):
+        self.check(
+            """
+            # nosec-next-line B101
+            assert True; assert True
+        """,
+            [2],
+            specific=1,
+        )
+
+    def test_next_after_multiline_inline_directive(self):
+        self.check(
+            """
+            assert (  # nosec-next-line B101
+                True
+            )
+            assert True
+            assert True
+        """,
+            [1, 5],
+            specific=1,
+        )
+
+    def test_next_at_eof(self):
+        self.check("assert True\n# nosec-next-line\n", [1])
+
+    def test_next_target_without_final_newline(self):
+        self.check("# nosec-next-line\nassert True", [], nosec_count=1)
+
+    def test_statement_overlap_before_end(self):
+        self.check(
+            """
+            # nosec-begin B307
+            result = (
+            # nosec-end
+                eval('1')
+            )
+            eval('2')
+        """,
+            [6],
+            specific=1,
+        )
+
+    def test_begin_in_multiline_statement(self):
+        self.check(
+            """
+            result = (
+            # nosec-begin B307
+                eval('1')
+            )
+            # nosec-end
+            eval('2')
+        """,
+            [6],
+            specific=1,
